---
title: "Why was the built glider tail-heavy?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

The built glider weighed what the model predicted but balanced 20 mm further
aft. This reconciles the two, working from the article back to the model rather
than forward.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Specified
Measured on the built glider and its material by the user, 2026-08-30/31:
**16 g all-up**, balancing **164.0 mm** aft of the nose with a 1p at 24 mm;
**wing leading edge 91 mm** aft of the nose; bevels **4 mm at the leading edge,
10 mm at the trailing edge**, each tapered to a point; and **four A3 sheets of
foam weighing 87 g**.
:::

```{python}
MM = 1e3
M, XCG, PENNY, PENNY_X = 0.016, 0.1640, 3.56e-3, 0.0240
WING_LE, LE_W, TE_W = 0.091, 4.0, 10.0
SIGMA_BRIEF = 0.027 / (0.297 * 0.420)        # what the brief claimed

# The article, with the known coin stripped off.
m_built = M - PENNY
x_built = (M * XCG - PENNY * PENNY_X) / m_built

# The model as it stood: the brief's foam, and the wing where the plan put it.
pred = mass_properties()
old_m = pred.mass * SIGMA_BRIEF / sigma
old_x = pred.x_cg + (S_w * SIGMA_BRIEF) * (WING_LE - x_le_w) / old_m
new_x = pred.x_cg + (S_w * sigma) * (WING_LE - x_le_w) / pred.mass

# Bevels: a wedge w*t/2 off each edge, at the measured density.
rho = sigma / t_foam / 1e9
bev = [(span * MM * w * t_foam * MM / 2, x)
       for span, xle, xte in [(b_w, WING_LE, WING_LE + c_w),
                              (b_h, x_le_h, x_te_v),
                              (b_v, x_te_v - fin_c[0], x_te_v)]
       for w, x in [(LE_W, xle), (TE_W, xte)]]
m_bev = sum(v for v, _ in bev) * rho
x_bev = sum(v * x for v, x in bev) / sum(v for v, _ in bev)

after_m = pred.mass - m_bev
after_x = (pred.mass * new_x - m_bev * x_bev) / after_m
glue_m = m_built - after_m
glue_x = (m_built * x_built - after_m * after_x) / glue_m

# The ballast this chapter used to call for, on the brief's foam.
x_t = neutral_point() - 0.10 * c_w
old_ballast = old_m * (pred.x_cg - x_t) / x_t
new_ballast = ballast_for(x_t, 0.0)
```

**Answer.** Two errors, pulling opposite ways on mass and the same way on
balance, which is why the total looked right and the trim did not.

The foam is `{python} f"{(1 - sigma/SIGMA_BRIEF)*100:.0f}"`% lighter than the
brief said — `{python} f"{sigma*0.297*0.420*1e3:.2f}"` g per A3 measured against the
`{python} f"{SIGMA_BRIEF*0.297*0.420*1e3:.0f}"` g claimed. The model was therefore carrying about
`{python} f"{(old_m - pred.mass)*1e3:.1f}"` g of foam that does not exist,
spread over the whole airframe. Against that, the build carries roughly
`{python} f"{glue_m*1e3:.1f}"` g of hot glue that the model does not carry at
all, and its centre of mass sits `{python} f"{glue_x*MM:.0f}"` mm aft of the
nose — behind the balance point, because the heaviest beads are at the
stabiliser and fin joints.

Phantom foam removed from everywhere and real glue added at the tail nearly
cancel in total mass. They do not cancel in moment. That is the whole
discrepancy: `{python} f"{(m_built - old_m)*1e3:+.2f}"` g of mass but
`{python} f"{(x_built - old_x)*MM:+.1f}"` mm of balance.

The bevels are real — `{python} f"{m_bev*1e3:.2f}"` g, some
`{python} f"{m_bev/pred.mass*100:.0f}"`% of the airframe — but they worked
*against* the shift. Weighted by edge length they remove foam centred
`{python} f"{x_bev*MM:.0f}"` mm aft of the nose, behind the balance point, so
taking that material off pulled the CG forward. Nor was the wing misplaced: at
91 mm it is `{python} f"{(x_le_w - WING_LE)*MM:.1f}"` mm *forward* of where the
plan put it, which widens the gap rather than closing it.

**What changed in the model.** `sigma` is now the measured
`{python} f"{sigma*1e3:.1f}"` g/m² rather than the brief's
`{python} f"{SIGMA_BRIEF*1e3:.1f}"`. Structure mass falls from
`{python} f"{old_m*1e3:.2f}"` g to `{python} f"{pred.mass*1e3:.2f}"` g and the
nose ballast for 10% MAC from `{python} f"{old_ballast*1e3:.2f}"` g to
`{python} f"{new_ballast*1e3:.2f}"` g. The
neutral point does not move at all — areal density never enters the
aerodynamics. Glue is still not modelled; the measurement above is recorded in
`_model.py` as a budget, not folded into the build-up, because one aircraft is
not a rule.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-reconcile
#| tbl-cap: "From the model as it stood to the glider on the bench. Mass and balance are reconciled together; neither alone identifies the cause."
import pandas as pd

pd.DataFrame({
    "step": ["model, as it stood (27 g/A3)", "foam corrected to 21.75 g/A3",
             "wing at its measured 91 mm", "less the bevels",
             "plus unmodelled glue", "the glider, measured"],
    "mass [g]": [f"{old_m*1e3:.2f}", f"{pred.mass*1e3:.2f}",
                 f"{pred.mass*1e3:.2f}", f"{after_m*1e3:.2f}",
                 f"{m_built*1e3:.2f}", f"{m_built*1e3:.2f}"],
    "balance [mm]": [f"{old_x*MM:.1f}", f"{pred.x_cg*MM:.1f}", f"{new_x*MM:.1f}",
                     f"{after_x*MM:.1f}", f"{x_built*MM:.1f}", f"{x_built*MM:.1f}"],
    "note": ["the prediction that was wrong", "19% less foam, balance unmoved",
             "2.4 mm forward — widens the gap",
             f"{m_bev*1e3:.2f} g off, centred {x_bev*MM:.0f} mm — pulls forward",
             f"{glue_m*1e3:.2f} g at {glue_x*MM:.0f} mm — pulls aft",
             "16.00 g all-up with the 1p"],
}).style.hide(axis="index")
```
